 North Dakota approves health insurance rate increases for 2027 ACA plans 
 ND Insurance Commissioner Jon Godfread (KFYR-TV) By Atticus Pead Published : Oct. 19, 2026 at 10:53 AM CDT | Updated : 45 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google BISMARCK, N.D. (KFYR) - If you buy your own health insurance in North Dakota, your bill is likely going up again next year.
 The North Dakota Insurance Department has approved average rate increases for 2027 Affordable Care Act plans, with individual market averages rising 19% for Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Dakota, 7.03% for Sanford Health Plan and 13.27% for Medica.
 Small-group plans, often used by small businesses, will also see substantial increases, with approved averages ranging from 9.5% to 18.34%.
 Insurance Commissioner Jon Godfread said rising health care costs are the primary driver.
 “Labor is costing more. Products and services are costing more,” Godfread said in an interview.
 The 2027 increases follow several years of high increases. In 2025, the state-approved average for Blue Cross Blue Shield individual plans rose 15.94%, while Sanford rose 16.5%. From 2020 to 2024, most averages were flat or up by single digits, and 2020 rates even decreased.
 Godfread said about 45,000 North Dakotans buy coverage outside an employer, Medicare or Medicaid and are directly affected by the individual and small-group ACA rates. He said the trend is also a strong indicator for private employer coverage.
 What was requested vs. what was approved: 
 Insurance companies submit requested rates to the department throughout the year. State law gives the commissioner authority to approve or adjust those requests.
 This year, Godfread cut three requests and approved four as requested.
 2027 ACA Individual Market - average rate changes:
 Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Dakota 21.40% 19.00% 
 Sanford Health Plan 7.03% 7.03% 
 Medica Health Plan 17.01% 13.27% 
 Approved average with full range in parentheses: BCBSND 19% (14.2% to 23.1%); Sanford 7.03% (1.52% to 10.95%); Medica 13.27% (-0.25% to 25.72%). 
 Averages are base-rate changes, not your personal premium. Your change depends on plan, age and location. 
 2027 ACA Small Group Market - average rate changes: 
 UnitedHealthcare Insurance Company 11.28% 11.28% 
 Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Dakota 9.50% 9.50% 
 Sandford Health Plan 18.34% 18.34% 
 Medica Insurance Company 18.96% 17.49% 
 Approved average with full range: UHC 11.28% (6.49% to 12.68%); BCBSND 9.5% (6.4% to 12.6%); Sanford 18.34% (13.21% to 26.57%); Medica 17.49% (10.56% to 19.98%). 
 Averages are base-rate changes, not your personal premium. Your change depends on plan, age and location. 
 Why not force rates lower? 
 Godfread said his office reviews insurer financials quarterly, including past claims, expected future claims, administrative expenses and profit, and is required to ensure companies remain able to pay claims. Federal rules require at least 80% of premium dollars go to claims; he said the state tries to keep that closer to 90%.
 “I can’t force companies to offer insurance in the state,” Godfread said. “If it’s not going to be financially viable for them to do it, they’ll exit the marketplace.”
 “I’m not sure we’d have much of a health insurance marketplace left to then offer to our citizens, and that’s a big concern as well,” he added.
 He said North Dakota still has three carriers on the individual market, more than some states with only one or two, and described it as a stable market facing significant rate pressure.
 “We are seeing a lot of rate pressure for consumers,” Godfread said.
 Transparency: 
 Godfread said he can track almost every dollar inside an insurance company, but not where the money goes after it leaves the insurer to hospitals and other providers.
 “Somebody needs to have that viewpoint of what are the hospitals charging, why are they charging, what do their financials look like?” Godfread said.
 “When you go to the hospital, it’s one of the only services where you don’t have any idea what that bill is going to be. And that’s a big problem,” he said.
 He pointed to the state’s last major health care cost study in 2019, which required a law to access hospital financial data for a two-year period, and said he wants lawmakers to renew that work to address affordability.
 “We’re not going to solve health insurance premiums if we don’t solve the health care cost issue,” he said.
 What to do: 
 Open enrollment for ACA plans begins Nov. 1 and runs through Jan. 15.
 Enroll by Dec. 15 for coverage starting Jan. 1.
 Plans can be reviewed at Healthcare.gov or through a licensed agent.
 Godfread encouraged shoppers to compare options and work with a licensed agent, noting that switching plans or tiers can change costs, deductibles, provider networks and out-of-pocket limits.
